title: Incompressible MPM and LSDEM sphere volume-fraction IBM validation

processes: fully resolved SDF volume-fraction immersed-boundary coupling
fluid force and torque on a fixed rigid LSDEM sphere
governing_assumptions: fictitious fluid remains inside the moving-particle domain
mixed density and density-weighted solid fraction follow Lai et al. equations 18-21
fluid-to-particle resultant follows Lai et al. equations 22-23 and 28

geometry.description: A radius-0.05 LSDEM sphere fixed inside a 0.4 by 0.2 by 0.24 rectangular tank; the analytical kernel test uses a centered sphere in a unit cube.

discretization.particle_or_template_resolution: one MPM point per cell; LSDEM SDF template spacing 0.05 before radius scaling and extent 9; sphere D/dx=10
discretization.refinement_plan: Production-kernel sphere fraction and pressure-resultant checks use D/dx=4, 8, and 16. Lai et al. test settling at D/dx=3 through 18 and report convergence around D/dx>=15; a settling/drag benchmark must therefore repeat the end-to-end model through at least D/dx=16 before a production claim.

time.stability_policy: The coupled critical-step check may reduce the requested timestep; reduced PCG/MGPCG comparison runs to 0.0004 s.

capacities.basis: The single fixed rigid body is an exact count; MPM, SDF-grid, and surface allocations retain separate positive margins.

fields: MPM particle position, velocity, and pressure

validation.observable: relative error of the SDF-integrated fixed-sphere pressure resultant at D/dx=16
validation.evidence: production Taichi SDF, pressure-gradient, and Eq. 28 device functions

invariants.basis: Eq. 30 is first-order interface reconstruction; 2% is required at D/dx=16.
The D/dx=16 relative error must be no more than one quarter of the D/dx=4 error.
PCG and MGPCG solve the same discrete pressure system to 1e-10 tolerance; end-state relative L2 differences must remain below 1e-4.

assumptions: The sphere STL is treated as the repository's near-unit-radius LSDEM template and scaled to radius 0.05 m.
The reduced solver comparison is a numerical equivalence test, not a terminal-settling validation.
